 West Virginia Basketball Preview: Mountaineers Host Mercer Looking to Stay Undefeated
 Published
 3 hours ago on
 November 12, 2026 
 By
 WV Sports Now 
 Mike Asti / WVSN 
 1 share 
 Share 
 Tweet 
 Reddit 
 Comments 
 The undefeated West Virginia Mountaineers (2-0) welcome the Southern Conference’s Mercer Bears (2-2) to Hope Coliseum on Thursday, November 12, 2026, for a non-conference clash.
 Early in the regular season, the Mountaineers have established a suffocating half court defense, boasting a massive points-allowed edge by yielding just 49.5 points per game. That physical resistance will dictate the terms of engagement against a Mercer squad that pushes the pace but struggles to protect the rim, surrendering 82.0 points per contest on the other end. This matchup will test whether the Bears possess the offensive discipline and firepower to crack West Virginia’s imposing defensive wall in a hostile Morgantown environment.
 West Virginia’s Outlook
 Head coach Ross Hodge’s squad enters this home contest aiming to build on a dominant 91-53 victory over Stetson. The Mountaineers executed their halfcourt sets efficiently in that matchup, shooting 50.0 percent from the field and connecting on 41.9 percent of their three-point attempts. West Virginia controlled the glass with 46 rebounds, committed just seven turnovers, and showcased its rotation depth by generating 34 bench points in a remarkably clean performance.
 The offensive charge is spearheaded by backcourt catalyst Miles Sadler, who paces the team with 20.5 points and 7.5 assists per game while navigating the perimeter. Providing secondary scoring punch is Joson Sanon with a steady 13.5 points per contest. In the paint, center Mouhamed Sylla anchors the interior, contributing 10.5 points and a team-high 6.5 rebounds per outing to give the Mountaineers multiple reliable options out of their sets.
 Mercer’s Outlook
 Head coach Ryan Ridder brings a Mercer squad that prefers a faster tempo but has struggled heavily with perimeter efficiency. The Bears average a solid 82.5 points per game, leaning on an offensive attack that shoots 43.8 percent from the floor overall despite converting a dismal 27.8 percent from three-point range. Mercer remains active on the glass, pulling down 37.3 rebounds per contest, but they will need to value their possessions better after committing 13.5 turnovers a night against early-season pressure.

 The Bears’ offense flows through lead guard Quinton Perkins II, who orchestrates the attack with a team-high 16.3 points and 3.5 assists per game. Guard Derek Goodman provides secondary scoring, chipping in 12.5 points per contest. Up front, forward Karon Boyd poses a physical threat on the interior, averaging 11.5 points while pacing Mercer with 7.5 rebounds per outing to challenge opponents around the rim.
 Rankings
 Both West Virginia (2-0) and Mercer (2-2) enter this matchup unranked in the current AP Top 25 and Coaches Poll. While neither squad has garnered national poll attention early in the regular season, current resume metrics show the Bears holding a No. 66 RPI ranking, well ahead of the Mountaineers at No. 173.
 Gametime
 Tipoff is scheduled for Thursday, November 12, 2026, at 7:00 p.m. ET. The West Virginia Mountaineers will host this non-conference matchup against the Mercer Bears on their home floor at Hope Coliseum in Morgantown, West Virginia.
 TV
 Fans can stream the action live on ESPN+ when the Mountaineers and Bears tip off at 7:00 p.m. ET in Morgantown.
 Spread
 WVU is heavily favored by 26.5 and the over/under is 151.5. West Virginia has smothered opponents with relentless halfcourt defense, yielding a meager 49.5 points per game over its first two victories. Meanwhile, Mercer has struggled heavily on that end of the floor, surrendering 82.0 points per contest through four games. That vast discrepancy in points allowed, combined with the Mountaineers’ home-court advantage at Hope Coliseum, should dictate the pricing.
